name: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026
short_description: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is an all-women half marathon, 10km, 5km and family-distance race at the National Stadium in Singapore on 1 November 2026.
ai_summary: Great Eastern Women's Run 2026 is an all-women road race at Singapore's National Stadium in The Kallang precinct on 1 November 2026. Organised by Great Eastern, it centres on a 21.1km Half Marathon alongside 10km and 5km categories, plus a 2km "Mummy+Me" run for mothers and daughters and a 100m "Princess Dash" for young girls.
pros: Women-only race with more than 12,000 runners in 2025
Four-hour cut-off for the half marathon
10 km, 5 km and 2 km run entirely on closed roads in 2025
Finish on the National Stadium track, with a breakfast box and a powder room for finishers
Pacers from 2:00 to 2:45 in the half marathon
cons: Humid from the start: 27°C with a 25°C dew point at 5am in 2025
Sheares Bridge just after 14 km makes the half marathon harder than it used to be
Sold out by early August in 2025
No race-pack collection: packs are couriered to a Singapore address

research_highlights: Route starts and finishes at Singapore Sports Hub/National Stadium; the 2025 edition's half marathon route passed the Barrage, Marina Bay and Gardens by the Bay, with an elevation section over Sheares Bridge just after the 14km mark noted as new and challenging for many runners.
Half marathon flag-off has typically been very early (around 5:15am), with runners arriving 45 minutes to an hour beforehand to enter the start pens.
Weather is consistently reported as warm and humid at race time, even in the early morning hours, based on multiple year's reviews (2024, 2025 editions).

The event is known for generous post-race and race-village perks: past editions have included free-flow oat milk, yoghurt, cheese, 100PLUS drinks, breakfast boxes, a 'powder room' for freshening up, and massage stations (though massage queues can be long).

Race has multiple categories including 21.1km (Elite/Open), 10km, 5km, a 2km Mummy & Me, and a 100m Princess Dash for young girls, and past editions sold out (fully subscribed) well ahead of race day.
research_watchouts: Massage stations at the race village have had very long queues in past editions, making them impractical for some runners.
Humid, sticky conditions at flag-off time have been repeatedly noted by participants, even in the early morning hours before sunrise.
New elevation additions to the half-marathon course (e.g., Sheares Bridge introduced in a past edition) can catch runners off guard if they haven't trained for elevation.
Some hydration-station gels have differed in brand from what runners are used to, so those with specific nutrition needs may want to carry their own.

faqs.question: Is the Great Eastern Women's Run open to men?
faqs.answer: No. The Great Eastern Women's Run is an all-women event: the 21.1 km, 10 km and 5 km are for women, the 2 km Mummy and Me pairs mothers with daughters aged 5 to 12, and the 100 m Princess Dash is for girls aged 3 to 6. Men come out to cheer along the route instead.

faqs.question: What time does the Great Eastern Women's Run start?
faqs.answer: Race listings give a 4.30am start for 1 November 2026 at the National Stadium in The Kallang, but the organiser's own category schedule could not be read. In 2025 the elite half marathon started at 5.00am, the open half marathon at 5.15am, the 10 km at 6.15am and the 5 km at 7.15am.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at the Great Eastern Women's Run?
faqs.answer: Five distances are offered, all for women and girls: a 21.1km Half Marathon, a 10km, a 5km, a 2km "Mummy+Me" run, and a 100m "Princess Dash" for young girls. This spread makes the event suitable for competitive runners, casual participants, and families attending together at the same race morning.
